comment: Integration cases, shared by run.py (golden records) and run_dual_decode.py (colour equivalence).
`mode` picks the CLI subcommand: `video` decodes a plain clip with OpenCV, `replay` re-feeds a
lossless FFV1 recording frame for frame. It is stated per case rather than sniffed from the file
extension, because the two are independent -- a `.mkv` may be either an FFV1 recording or an
ordinary compressed clip -- and the mode is also what decides whether a case has a YUV -> RGB
conversion to vary at all.
`frame_resize` is REQUIRED on every case and states the pipeline configuration the case runs under:
true = the shipped frame-resize band (the forwarded frame's anchor unit is held inside the band named by
kDefaultFrameResizeMinUnit/MaxUnit in native/src/core/pipeline_config.h -- 540-720 px today; scaled up
below the lower bound, scaled down only once the unit reaches Frame::kShrinkDeadband times the UPPER
bound (1.5 x 720 = 1080 px today, see native/src/cv/frame.h), left alone in between -- so a unit just
above 720 is NOT resized), false = no resize at all. Both runners pass the
corresponding CLI flag EXPLICITLY (`--frame-resize` / `--no-frame-resize`) rather than relying on the
CLI's default, for two independent reasons: a reader of this manifest must be able to see what a case
was recognised under without opening a runner, and the suite's configuration must not move silently the
next time somebody changes what the CLI defaults to. run.py REFUSES a case that omits the key, so a new
case cannot be added without saying which configuration it is a baseline for.
Every case here states true, because that is what the app ships: the suite's baseline is the shipped
configuration, not a configuration kept alive only by the goldens. The band's NUMBERS deliberately live
in the C++ constants and not in this file -- a manifest carrying its own bounds would keep passing after
the shipped band moved.
`anchor_unit` is REQUIRED on every case too, and is the geometry that must actually REACH RECOGNITION:
the anchor unit -- the intersection width, the one number every normalized coordinate is multiplied by --
of every frame the scraper scraped. Both runners read it off the CLI's run summary (`forwarded_frames`,
`anchor_unit_min`, `anchor_unit_max`) and require min == max == this value, i.e. the run held ONE geometry
throughout and it was this one. It exists because `frame_resize: true` above states an INTENTION and
nothing was checking the outcome: back when the band did clamp this material (~736 -> 720), that step
changed no record on any clip here (all 18 goldens regenerated byte-identical through it), so a band that
was never armed, or that stopped applying, left every golden green -- measured, all three ways, in
testdata/evidence/android-web-import/handover/B4a-goldens-through-band.md. The clamp no longer happens on
this material (see the shrink dead band below), which is exactly why the field still has to be here: what
geometry reached recognition is invisible in the records either way.
THIS IS AN OBSERVATION, NEVER AN INPUT, and that is what keeps the bounds in C++. The number here is not
passed to the CLI and cannot configure anything -- the CLI is told a BOOLEAN (`--frame-resize`) and
resolves the band from kDefaultFrameResizeMinUnit/MaxUnit. So moving the shipped band turns every case
red and CANNOT be made green by editing C++ alone; the manifest has to be re-stated, per case, where a
reviewer sees it. The direction of authority is C++ decides, this file observes.
735-737 per case, and each case states its OWN number, because that is the width its clip enters at and
no arm of the band transforms it: the shrink arm is gated by Frame::kShrinkDeadband and does not fire
until the unit reaches 1080 px, and 735-737 is nowhere near either bound. That makes the suite an
exercise of the band's PASS-THROUGH only; the scale-DOWN and scale-UP arms have no integration coverage
(see the note above for the material that would provide it), and stating this number per case is what
makes that visible rather than assumed. The values were 720 on all 18 until the dead band was added; they
are re-stated here, per case, exactly as the direction-of-authority rule above requires.
LOSING THE SCALE-DOWN ARM'S REAL-FOOTAGE COVERAGE IS A DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT (2026-08-19, user):
the arm's boundary is pinned by unit tests instead -- test/cv/test_frame.cpp exercises 1079/1080/1081 at
two different upper bounds, so the threshold is fixed as a RATIO and not as a literal -- and that was
judged sufficient. Do not file the gap again; if you want it back, the material to use is the 1080-wide
regression grid, which is not registered in ctest.
`golden` is the committed record baseline run.py compares against. A case MAY omit it, and then no
integration_golden ctest is registered for it and it takes part in the dual-decode suite only.
landscape_2pane_ps5 is the one such case. WHAT THE NAME REFERS TO IS THE GEOMETRY, and the geometry is
faithful: the frame is a 2326x1340 canvas of the size a two-pane browser share produces, and the detail
dialog sits where the GAME puts it when the game itself is displaying two panes. What the clip does not
reproduce is everything OUTSIDE that dialog -- measured across every frame, the non-black bounding box
is a single 738x1310 region and the column-mean profile carries no pane divider, because the
surrounding pane content was never composited in. Read the name as a statement about where the dialog
is, not about how much of the screen is filled.
What the case is for is COLOUR, not layout: its header-green probe reads G=194 under BT.601 and G=174
under BT.709, i.e. across isHeaderGreen's former `g >= 180`. It latches no pane under BT.709 and
produces zero records, which is the defect the dual-decode suite exists for and which no portrait clip
here can show. It carries
no golden on purpose: the clip is a locally derived transcode of an FFV1 mimic-player source, so its
exact pixels depend on the local libx264 build and a committed record baseline would be a false
regression alarm elsewhere. The bt601-vs-bt709 equivalence is instead a property of whatever file
sits at that path, which is why that is the contract stated for it.
THE `_toppad` SUFFIX ON BOTH LANDSCAPE FILES IS A CORRECTED GEOMETRY (2026-08-18). The earlier pair
padded the WRONG EDGE: the content sat flush against row 0 with 30 black rows at the BOTTOM, which is a
combination a browser window share cannot produce -- the window decoration puts its padding at the TOP
and the game content runs to the frame's bottom edge. The correction is a PURE TRANSLATION of those 30
rows from the bottom to the top at unchanged frame size, and the vacated top rows are filled BLACK
rather than with a drawn title bar, which would be inventing pixels nothing ever measured (nothing
outside the dialog takes part in recognition). User's finding and user's decision; the previous files
are left in place untouched and these cases name the new ones.
`anchor_unit` is UNCHANGED by that correction: the unit is the intersection WIDTH, and a vertical
translation moves both vertical landmarks by the same 30 rows, so the solved scale (737.11) is identical
either way. It reads 737 rather than 720 for an unrelated reason -- the shrink dead band, above -- which
is what stopped the band from clamping it; the padding correction has nothing to do with that number.
firefox_landscape_2pane_ps5 is the same landscape import as decoded by a real desktop Firefox 153,
recorded losslessly (FFV1/bgr0) and replayed. READ ITS PROVENANCE EXACTLY: the file is that browser
dump WITH ITS ROWS TRANSLATED AFTERWARDS by the same +30, NOT a fresh browser run, so it is not
frame-for-frame what Firefox handed over. What is preserved is the browser's pixel data -- the dump's
rows 0..1309 are bit-identical at rows 30..1339, verified per frame on all 374. What is discarded is
the h264 ringing of up to 10/255 that sat on the dump's rows 1310..1313, outside the content's bounding
box and outside every probe. It DOES carry a golden, unlike the clip above, because it is still a
frozen artefact rather than
a locally regenerated transcode -- its pixels are bytes in the file, so the record set is reproducible
on any machine that holds it. It exists because a browser's decoder is not `--color_matrix bt709`:
it differs in rounding as well, and 4 to 5 units of that rounding on one 4:2:0 chroma-shared row was
enough to make this import produce zero records while every dual-decode case stayed green: nominal
bt709 still cleared the old `g - b >= 120` on that row, by 0 on the worst column. See the note on
`g - b` in src/cv/detail_crop_calibrator.h and the reproduction steps in test/README.md.
player_standard_switch_at_factor_top and player_inheritance_switch_with_tiny_scroll are the first two
MUST-FIRE cases: a character switch made ON the factor tab, before that tab was captured, which only
CharaDetailSceneScraper::maybeResetOnFactorChange (Rule 3) can detect -- the record type does not change,
so Rule 0 cannot, and the tab is not complete, so Rule 2 cannot. Every other case here is a MUST-NOT-RESET
case, so without these two the gate's positive half had no automated cover at all. What they assert is the
reset only THROUGH the record set: each golden holds exactly one record, and that record is the SECOND
character's -- a gate that stopped firing would fold both characters into one session and change it.
The inheritance case is the harder one: both entries are the same character (same name, same portrait,
same InheritanceOnly record type) and differ only in their factor list.
player_standard_factor_only_1, player_standard_factor_tiny_scroll_switch and _2 are the remaining three
MUST-FIRE clips, and their correct outcome is ZERO records: no character in them is ever shown on all the
tabs a record needs. They therefore state `expect_records` instead of a `golden`, and a deliberate
`expect_errors` / `expect_discarded` beside it. What each field buys, in the order that matters:
* `expect_discarded` -- the number of sessions thrown away mid-run, i.e. the RESET COUNT (1 / 2 / 4).
This is the only thing these clips can assert about the gate: they produce zero records with
maybeResetOnFactorChange in place AND with it ripped out (measured), so a record baseline of [] would
go green against a build in which Rule 3 does not exist. The reset count would not.
* `expect_errors` -- the terminal error tag the run must announce, so that an empty result is a run that
SAID it was empty. closed_before_completed for all three: the session ended before it completed, and
the core reports that one way whether the clip ran out with the detail screen still open
(factor_only_1, via NativeApi::endOfInput) or the screen returned to the list (the other two). Its
presence is what separates an announced emptiness from a silent one -- the distinction the exit code
also carries -- and factor_only_1 is the only case in the manifest whose tag can only be produced by
the end-of-input path, so a broken endOfInput fails THAT case by name.
* `expect_records: 0` -- the count itself, checked both against the files on disk and against the count
the core states in its run summary.
They carry NO golden: a committed two-byte [] would be a baseline that asserts nothing, and stating the
expectation as data keeps the fact and its meaning in one place. They also take no part in the dual-decode
suite (bt601 == bt709 over two empty sets is a pass-by-vacuum), and skip there with that reason named.
See testdata/evidence/android-web-import/cpp/fix1-golden-intent.md for what each clip contains and for
the measurement behind the paragraph above.
`expect_discarded_incomplete` is stated by EVERY case, because omitting it states zero and zero is a real
expectation -- the same convention `expect_errors` uses. It is the count of sessions thrown away BEFORE
they produced their record, i.e. the run's own answer to `did this import lose anything?`, and it is a
different number from `expect_discarded`: an ordinary character switch made after a character completed
is a discard that lost nothing and is reported as such. Nothing here pinned it before, and the regression
it catches lands on the HEALTHY clips: a build that stopped setting the discard's `completed` bit would
leave every record, every golden and every `expect_discarded` untouched while reclassifying every clean
character switch as a lost session -- which is what the app's partial-import card is built from, so the
user would be told a clean import lost characters. The two must-fire cases that produce a record state 1
(the record is the SECOND character's, so the first character's session was lost before completing); the
three zero-record cases state their whole reset count, since a run that completes nothing loses every
session it discards; every other case leaves it at the default zero by not stating it.
Videos live under testdata/clips/golden/ and are NOT committed; goldens ARE committed (baseline).
A case whose video is absent is skipped, so this manifest may list more clips than any one
machine has locally. Add a case here + regenerate its golden with run.py --update-golden.
